article_title: A Procedural Guide to Cognitive Task Analysis: The PARI Methodology.:
citation: Ellen P. Hall, Sherrie P. Gott, Robert A. Pokorny. (1995). A Procedural Guide to Cognitive Task Analysis: The PARI Methodology. Armstrong Laboratory, Human Resources Directorate, Brooks AFB, Texas. AL/HR-TR-1995-0108
title: BJS cognitive architecture: procedural, declarative (system), and strategic knowledge
description: The report's organizing framework decomposes complex problem-solving performance into three coordinated knowledge components. As quoted from Gott (1989): "The knowledge and processes that constitute that performance are (a) procedural (or how- to-do-it) knowledge, (b) declarative (domain) knowledge of the object (often called system or device knowledge), and (c) strategic (or how- to-decide-what-to-do-and-when) knowledge." Strategic knowledge serves an executive control function, deploying procedural and device knowledge via goals, plans, and decision rules to enable dynamic, opportunistic reasoning. The PARI methodology is designed to capture all three components and their coordinated deployment.
requirements: Analysis must situate knowledge elicitation in authentic problem-solving contexts, since strategic knowledge is overlooked when domain knowledge is analyzed outside its intended use
constraints: The framework targets ill-structured problem-solving domains such as fault diagnosis, where no well-defined algorithm for solution exists
target_learners: Technical trainees acquiring complex troubleshooting expertise
target_learning_goals: Integration of procedural, system, and strategic knowledge for adaptive problem solving
examples: Figure 1 of the report depicts the BJS Cognitive Architecture showing interactions among strategic, system, and procedural knowledge
